summary: Add marketing_opt_in as a nullable boolean column with DEFAULT False on account_user, backfill existing rows, deploy new version with state_only migration, retire old version, then contract the column to NOT NULL. The DEFAULT False ensures old version inserts receive False, preventing NULLs during concurrent traffic.
write_consistency: The column is created with a database DEFAULT False; therefore the old version's INSERT statements (which omit the unknown column) will store False. The new version explicitly sets marketing_opt_in to False. After retire_old, the column is altered to NOT NULL, and all rows contain False, satisfying the no-NULL requirement throughout the overlap and after.

stages.description: Add nullable marketing_opt_in column with DEFAULT False.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN marketing_opt_in boolean NULL DEFAULT false;

stages.description: Backfill marketing_opt_in to False for remaining NULLs.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET marketing_opt_in = False WHERE marketing_opt_in IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version; it stops serving traffic.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN marketing_opt_in SET NOT NULL;
